subsystems.name: Gas-handling system
subsystems.role: mixes the reducing atmosphere to be irradiated, in controlled proportions.
parts: gas cylinders (nitrogen, methane, sometimes carbon monoxide, hydrogen, water vapour)

subsystems.name: Energy source
subsystems.role: supplies the energy that breaks methane and nitrogen apart.
parts: ultraviolet lamps or excimer light sources

subsystems.name: Reaction chamber
subsystems.role: where radicals recombine into ever-larger molecules and condense into particles.
parts: flow tube or reactor vessel with cold walls
temperature control down to cryogenic levels

subsystems.name: Aerosol collection
subsystems.role: gathers the solid product for analysis.

subsystems.name: Analytical suite
subsystems.role: identifies what the haze is made of.

subsystems.name: Hydrolysis bench
subsystems.role: simulates contact with liquid water, the step that could turn haze into biological building blocks.

subsystems.name: Optical measurement and modelling
subsystems.role: turns the product into data other scientists can use.
parts: spectrophotometer or ellipsometer for refractive index and absorption
radiative-transfer models of Titan and of exoplanet atmospheres

buildSteps.title: Choose the gas mixture
buildSteps.detail: Decide what to simulate — modern Titan, the early Earth, or an exoplanet — and set nitrogen and methane proportions, from a few per mille to several per cent methane, with or without carbon monoxide or water.

buildSteps.title: Pull a vacuum and set the flow
buildSteps.detail: The chamber is pumped down and the gas mixture is fed at a controlled rate, typically a few tens of standard cubic centimetres per minute at millibar pressures, so the mixture is continuously refreshed.

buildSteps.title: Ignite the discharge or lamp
buildSteps.detail: A plasma at watts to tens of watts, or an ultraviolet beam, breaks methane and nitrogen into radicals and ions.

buildSteps.title: Grow the aerosol
buildSteps.detail: The radicals recombine into heavier molecules, which nucleate into solid particles tens to hundreds of nanometres across; residence time in the chamber sets how far the chemistry gets.

buildSteps.title: Collect the solid
buildSteps.detail: Particles settle on cold surfaces and are scraped or rinsed off, producing a brown, powdery analogue of Titan's haze.

buildSteps.title: Split and hydrolyse
buildSteps.detail: Part of the sample is kept whole; the rest is sealed with water or strong acid and heated, then dried and derivatised so that amino acids and nucleobases become detectable.

buildSteps.title: Analyse the molecules
buildSteps.detail: Mass spectrometry, chromatography and infrared or Raman spectroscopy identify individual compounds and the overall complexity of the mixture.

buildSteps.title: Measure optical properties
buildSteps.detail: Thin films of the analogue are measured for refractive index and absorption across ultraviolet, visible and infrared wavelengths.

buildSteps.title: Feed the results back
buildSteps.detail: The molecular inventory and optical constants go into models of Titan's haze and of exoplanet spectra, and are compared with spacecraft measurements.

prerequisites.why: compact discharge reactors and lamps let a lab mimic upper-atmosphere chemistry on a bench.
the products are a hugely complex mixture; sorting them out needs precise mass measurement.
the Cassini orbiter and the Huygens probe, which descended through the atmosphere in 2005, provided the haze's real composition and optical properties for comparison.
every laboratory's analogue differs with its gas mix and energy source, so results are hard to compare across groups.
haze effects in exoplanet atmospheres are now measurable but still hard to disentangle from clouds.

pathway.milestone: laboratory analogues made in plasma and ultraviolet reactors, hydrolysed and analysed by mass spectrometry
pathway.unlocks: evidence that abiotic aerosols can release amino acids such as glycine and alanine.

pathway.milestone: standardised, shared sample libraries and round-robin comparisons between laboratories
pathway.unlocks: results that can be compared directly instead of being laboratory-specific.

pathway.milestone: NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft reaches Titan in the mid-2030s
pathway.unlocks: direct analysis of real haze and surface organics to test the laboratory findings.

pathway.milestone: interpreting haze in exoplanet spectra, including the risk of mistaking abiotic chemistry for a biological signature
pathway.unlocks: reliable reading of atmospheric data for signs of life elsewhere.

pathway.milestone: returning a Titan sample to Earth
pathway.unlocks: the full power of terrestrial instruments on genuine prebiotic material.
